I'm not exactly sure how to express what I'm hoping to get out of voat, but I'll try...

My concern whenever people start to bail on major sites is that the funny people and the people who think 'free speech' means being allowed to be extremely cruel to other users will all end up in the same new site, and there won't be a buffer of moderate or compassionate people to make the new community pleasant to use. A lot of what I find funny is somewhat cruel or shocking, so I'm not interested in a 'safe space,' but I do want to be able to participate in a community without feeling completely alienated or abused as a woman. Basically I want to hang out online with funny people who can act like adults when necessary, which of course is a lot to ask for. I've been reading 4chan for like seven years maybe, and I've been a reddit user since like 2009 or something, and I'm kind of grumpy about having to learn a new thing. But the little I've seen of this community so far has been very positive, and I'm looking forward to learning the culture.

Weelcome aboard.

You know, the funny thing is that you don't see too many people around here trying to be edgy for the sake of being edgy. Oh, I'm not saying we don't have some bad apples, but no more than anywhere else. If anything, I see more people to discussing ideas, and less likely to shout down opposing views. Not sure how long it's going to last, but if we all do our part we can make it part of the culture.

So pick some land, build something great and welcome to Voat!

I can definitely understand what you're saying. I absolutely love edgy and offensive humor, it's the best way to get through the shit parts of life, so I'm not a fan of the constantly offended crowd. But I'm also not a fan of just genuine assholes.

I've been on here for a while now and lurked for months before that, and I can honestly say this was the kinda place I was looking for. Of course you're going to get the extremes anywhere you go, but for the most part people tend to respect each others space here. More controversial things are generally kept in their own subs (which users can block if they want), and when it's in the main subs it's overwhelmingly genuine back and forth discussion rather than spewing hateful shit around.

Just a random example of one of the more controversial (for lack of a better word), subs. During the Fatpeoplehate exodus a few weeks ago, they voluntarily had themselves removed from /v/all. They weren't forced to or even asked to, they requested it themselves because they didn't want to dominate content for everyone else.

I wouldn't worry about that too much. He was very much at risk of this in 2008 (when SpaceX and Tesla were both on the verge of going out of business), but he seems to have made it over the hump now. Most of his major initiatives are funded with the cash of others at this point, and there seems to be no shortage of people lining up to invest in his ideas for a better future. He has a launch backlog of years for SpaceX, and a production backlog of years for Tesla cars and Tesla Energy stationary battery packs. That doesn't even count the side benefits of his initiatives like his Gigafactories selling batteries to third parties (which will be substantial). Even Solar City is breaking new ground creating massive new financial instruments to roll out solar more quickly and easily to end users everywhere. Even the futuristic Hyperloop is likely to make mad cash as soon as the proof-of-concept is developed and it actually exists in meat-space. They already have companies/governments clamoring for the tech around the world. Expect super-fast electric VTOL aircraft as his next major initiative once the Hyperloop gets rolling and I expect the reaction to that technology will be equally huge as airports will be able to shrink dramatically in size allowing placement in all kinds of locations formerly too small or remote for large aircraft service.

Plus his ROI to date has been impressive and truly massive. He is now worth nearly 12 billion and that is just going in increase substantially as his companies grow and his new initiatives get rolling. He has the very good possibility of becoming the world's wealthiest man within the next two decades for sure. I expect to see articles about him having "the Midas touch" within ten years.
